worker: app/scripts/opencode-assets.mjs (headless): the desktop OpencodeKernel, request transport, research pack, completion certificate and research collector, compiled from this checkout at worker start
account: the owner's own desktop account, read in process memory by an owner-authorized local launcher through the app's account-core + OS safeStorage (same approach as the earlier comparison launcher). The research profile reached the worker through a private FIFO, never a regular file; nothing secret was printed or written. Its refresh token was replaced by a placeholder so the worker could not rotate the desktop session; the launcher itself refreshed the session exactly as the app does (re-encrypted into the app's account file).
prompt: desktop i18n build.prompt, verbatim (the request the app sends automatically after a paper import)
stopCriterion: first completion line with status=complete (desktop programCertificate on the exact program bytes); otherwise at most 2 desktop-style Retry requests (same prompt); quit.

limits.spendEstimate: Haiku 5.5 long-prompt tier as an upper bound: $0.50/MTok input, $2.50/MTok output+reasoning; the hosted route reported cost=0 on every message, which is not evidence of free usage

identityCheck: GET /api/desktop/identity returns 404 in production (web research-collection endpoint not deployed, T13). The acceptance harness answered that one call locally from the desktop key's own signed claim (claim.u == Supabase user id); the hosted proxy still verified the key signature on every model request. This is a harness substitution, not a product change.

observationsNotFixed: Haiku marked its own evidence records verification='verified' in Tversky-Kahneman (e.g. a reconstructed 'Yes [88 percent] No [12 percent]' quote whose source order is 'No … Yes …'). The UI does not display 'verified' (installed walkthrough W6), but the stored field is agent self-report.

Tversky-Kahneman program has 0 steps (procedure is represented by 4 procedure nodes); minimum coverage passes. A runnable package would need steps. No views/artifacts were written in that run (the build prompt does not ask for them).
OCR noise is preserved verbatim in quotes (e.g. '113 percent]' for a printed '[13 percent]'); the agent filed a review issue for that disagreement instead of silently correcting the quote.
Reported input tokens (≈135k-245k per run) are far below the request volume (34-76 MB of JSON per run): the usage field appears to exclude cached prompt tokens. Cost here is an estimate, not a bill.

The rerun's last bash call (rm -f of two copied kit files) needed a permission outside Auto's heuristic; the supervisor rejected it, which ended the turn. The certificate was already complete; artifacts/ keeps hs-kit.css/js copies.
notCovered: The real-model build ran in the headless worker, not inside the installed app UI (installed walkthrough used a mock kernel; see installed-mac.json).
Long papers beyond 23 scanned pages; multiple-turn interrupted builds with a real model.
privacy: Projects, logs, sessions and the PDFs stay in a private local acceptance folder. This file contains only counts, hashes and quote prefixes of at most 60 characters.
